public_feedback.diagnostic:
Encrypted outputs failed the fixed numerical comparison.
Binding and shape guidance:
Reduce exactly the declared logical axes. Every non-reduced coordinate identifies a separate group, including batch, head, row and column coordinates. A rotate-and-add sums the source slots of that rotation, not automatically one logical group. For each output, retain only its own reduction members; exclude other groups, padded tails and repeated periodic copies. The sampled fibers below are logical C-order indices, not intermediate ciphertext slot plans. Choose and track your own intermediate slot mapping. A value valid at one lane must be moved or replicated before it is used at another lane. Mean divides by the full logical member count.
Reshape and flatten preserve logical C-order element indices. Permute and transpose change which logical coordinate occupies each flat index. Reshaping an object array rearranges whole Expr cells; it does not move encrypted slots inside those cells. Preserve the coordinate mapping through each transform and every later reduction or broadcast.
Broadcasting right-aligns logical axes and expands only singleton dimensions. For a product followed by a reduction, match both operand coordinates before contraction. Keep all non-reduced batch/head/row/column coordinates separate. Matching object-array shapes or selecting the same physical lane in different expressions does not establish matching logical coordinates.
Input annotations describe only the frozen input binding. Valid logical elements occupy their declared chunk prefix; padding is not another logical feature. A chunk can contain multiple logical rows or groups. Preserve their identities after projections and intermediate transforms. Intermediate ciphertext representations are your choice; named outputs still use the frozen selectors.
Only names in public_constants or the explicitly admitted public-weight interface are bound DSL globals. Names under model.constants are logical graph references, not implicit Python variables. Respect the actual bound scalar/vector contents and the exact logical-to-public scalar matches; p-number order has no semantic role. A single-lane packing mask or a masked reduction coefficient is not an all-lane gain, zero bias or replicated scalar. A logical public tensor still needs its declared coordinate mapping; a uniform tensor does not turn matmul into scalar multiplication.
Reduce the declared logical axes and elements. For periodic packing, admitted rotations can form a sum without extracting every scalar first. A sum valid only in slot zero is not a replicated ciphertext scalar. Exclude padded tails and unrelated rows; object reshape/transpose does not rotate or replicate encrypted slots.
A one-element encrypted tensor must occupy every required destination slot before a lane-wise broadcast. Distinguish replicated scalars, valid prefixes and padding. Equal object-array shapes do not establish equal ciphertext layouts. Preserve each named output binding.
A reduction produces exactly the declared reduced shape. Intermediate slot representation is your choice, but every later broadcast must use that same representation. A prefix scalar and a replicated scalar differ. Broadcast every declared dimension, including row/channel axes and across ciphertext chunks; exclude padding. Sum and mean differ by the full logical reduction count. Final outputs follow the frozen named C-order bindings.
